# venice-bridge

> venice-bridge is a free, open-source local bridge for macOS that lets OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex CLI and other OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible coding agents use a venice.ai web subscription, with working tool calls.

Unofficial: not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Venice.ai. It uses undocumented web endpoints and your own logged-in session, which may be against Venice's terms of service. Use your own account only. Version 0.4.0, MIT.

## What it does

- Two local processes. The bridge (`venice_bridge.py` plus `tolerant_parser.py`) serves OpenAI Chat Completions on `127.0.0.1:18891`: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (streaming and non-streaming), `GET /v1/models`, `GET /health`, `GET /stats`, `POST /reload`, `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`, `POST /v1/embeddings`, image tools (`POST /v1/images/generations`, `/v1/images/edits`, `/v1/image/upscale`, `/v1/image/background-remove`, `GET /v1/image/styles`; 0-credit models only unless `VENICE_ALLOW_CREDIT_IMAGES=1`). Chat accepts base64 image and document attachments.
- The optional adapter (`venice_adapters.py`, stdlib only) on `127.0.0.1:18892` translates Anthropic Messages (`POST /v1/messages`, `/v1/messages/count_tokens`) and OpenAI Responses (`POST /v1/responses`) to Chat Completions and forwards them to the bridge. That is how Claude Code and Codex CLI work.
- Forwards to the venice.ai web app's own backend with your browser login (`__client` cookie of `clerk.venice.ai`). No Venice API key. Tested on a paid Venice web plan (Pro).
- `VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE=auto` (default) uses Venice's plain chat route (no Venice agent loop, no swallowed calls) and falls back to the agent route for a model the chat route does not know; `chat` and `agent` force one route.
- Emulates tool calling in text (Venice's web routes hide client tools) and returns real OpenAI `tool_calls`, with a tolerant parser, native and tagged call readers, tool and argument routing, in-bridge retries, a judge for early stops, and a stream gate.
- Local models: a model id `<backend>/<model>` (e.g. `ollama/qwen3:8b`, `lmstudio/<id>`) goes straight to that local OpenAI-compatible server, with no Venice login, tool emulation or quota. Backends are configured in `~/.config/venice-bridge/backends.json`.
- Opt-in Venice web search: model suffix `:web` (web search and URL scraping) or `:xsearch` (X search), or `VENICE_WEB=1` / `VENICE_X_SEARCH=1`. Off by default.
- Opt-in reasoning on the chat route, only for requests that declare no tools: model suffix `:think` (aliases `:reason`, `:reasoning`; combinable, e.g. `:web:think`), `VENICE_REASONING=1`, or `reasoning_effort` `medium` / `high`. The chain of thought comes back as `reasoning_content` (message field; `delta.reasoning_content` when streaming). With tools, `:think`, `VENICE_REASONING` and `reasoning_effort` are all ignored, so reasoning has no effect in OpenCode / Claude Code / Codex agent loops and never causes the reasoning-content HTTP 400 there.
- Model list: `GET /v1/models` hides credit models and end-to-end-encrypted `e2ee-*` models; `VENICE_EXCLUDE_MODELS` hides more by glob. Hidden models can still be requested by id.
- `venice-auto` virtual model (listed first): the first Venice id in `VENICE_AUTO_MODELS` (default `deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored,ollama/qwen3:8b`), switching to the first local `<backend>/<model>` while the bridge knows the daily quota is used up. The request that hits the limit still fails once (`403` `venice_quota_exhausted`); the local backend must be running; `POST /reload` clears the over-quota state.
- Response cache: a byte-identical repeat request is answered from memory without a Venice call (`VENICE_BRIDGE_CACHE=0` disables).
- `temperature` and `top_p` are forwarded when the client sets them; `max_tokens` is ignored by the Venice route.

## Install

- Requirements: macOS, Python 3.10+, `pip install curl_cffi` (or `pipx install venice-bridge` from PyPI), and a client: OpenCode, the Claude Code CLI, Codex CLI, or any OpenAI Chat Completions client.
- Save the `__client` cookie value to `~/.config/venice-bridge/client-cookie.txt` (mode 600).
- Run `python3 venice_bridge.py`, check `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18891/health`.
- For Claude Code or Codex also run `python3 venice_adapters.py`, check `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18892/health`.

## Use

- OpenCode: copy the provider block from `examples/opencode.json` into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, then `opencode -m venice-bridge/deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored`.
- Claude Code: `ln -s "$PWD/claude-venice" ~/.local/bin/claude-venice`, then `claude-venice` or `claude-venice -m <venice-model-id>`. It uses an isolated profile `~/.claude-venice` and, by default, adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (Claude Code then runs tools without asking); opt out with `VENICE_CLAUDE_SKIP_PERMS=0` or your own `--permission-mode`.
- Codex CLI: `VB_KEY=local codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -c 'model_providers.vb={name="vb",base_url="http://127.0.0.1:18892/v1",wire_api="responses",env_key="VB_KEY"}' -c model_provider=vb -m deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored "<task>"`. Codex's namespace tools (MCP servers, multi-agent) and its built-in `web_search` do not pass through.
- Any OpenAI-compatible client: base URL `http://127.0.0.1:18891/v1`, any API key. From a Docker container: `http://host.docker.internal:18891/v1` (measured with Docker Desktop on macOS); no need to bind to 0.0.0.0.
- Autostart: `examples/com.example.venice-bridge.plist` and `examples/com.example.venice-adapters.plist` (launchd templates).
- Offline self-checks: `python3 test_venice_bridge.py` and `python3 test_venice_adapters.py`.

## Cost model

- The web plan is limited by a daily request quota, not by tokens. `usage` numbers are estimates (about 4 characters per token; Venice returns no token counts). Fewer requests save quota; shorter prompts do not. `/health` shows `chat_quota.remaining` and `resets_in_min`.
- The quota is plan-wide: every Venice model shares it. To keep working after it runs out, use `venice-auto` with a local fallback.

## Limits

- macOS only so far (Linux and Windows untested).
- With tools, short replies are sent only when complete. Tool calling is emulated; open models sometimes need a retry.
- Venice's fast models are weak at long agentic chains (measured on one machine, one account): good for cheap exploratory runs, not high-stakes work.
- The agent route needs a paid plan (a free account gets `403 creator_access_required`); a free account has a very small chat quota.
